revision: Working revision25: fabrication comparison with the original Eagle boards; B3F switch strips declared

mainboard.electrical_evidence_basis: Fresh KiCad10.0.7 reports for this revision; DRC violations, schematic parity and ignored checks exactly equal the previous fresh report. ERC0 under retained project rules.
mainboard.unconnected_track_end_note: The +5V pair (S22 pad 1) is closed by the B3F-40XX jumper pad groups: the original switch strips 1-2 bridge S19 and S22, as the original Eagle symbol draws them. The remaining GND pair is the original analog/digital ground split (IC9 pad 8 side vs the digital B.Cu track), an unrouted airwire in the original Eagle board, joined through the J3-J7 board-to-board wiring. KiCad names varying representative pads or tracks of the same two islands between runs. Copper is unchanged.

ioboard.electrical_evidence_basis: Fresh KiCad10.0.7 reports for this revision; DRC violations, schematic parity and ignored checks exactly equal the previous fresh report. ERC0 under retained project rules.
ioboard.unconnected_track_end_note: The GND pair (MIXOUT0 sleeve island vs the main ground track) is the original jack-ground island, an unrouted airwire in the original Eagle board, returned through J7 pin 2 to the mainboard analog ground. KiCad names varying representative pads or tracks of the same two islands between runs.

model_evidence_basis: No model path, model transform or footprint placement changed; the revision-24 native lead audit and nominal-fit findings apply unchanged.

fabrication_comparison.method: KiCad 10.0.7 Gerber/Excellon output compared object by object with the original Eagle 4.13 board geometry, read from the staging XML of the binary files and evaluated with Eagle 4.13 CAM rules (restring, elongation, stop frame); the XML was cross-checked against an independent read of original-eagle/.

scope: Jumper pad groups ("1" "2") and ("3" "4") on the 23 B3F-40XX switch placements and the project library footprint; footprint metadata only. Copper, pads, drills, nets, zones, footprint poses, models and the I/O project are unchanged. Adds the Gerber/drill comparison with the original Eagle boards and the review of the three recorded connection gaps.
limitations: Marking text is transcribed from one set of kit photographs; date and lot codes varied between kits.
Logos are omitted; Source Code Pro approximates the vendors' marking fonts; ink colour is illustrative.
The 74HC165 has no photograph and carries its part number only.
Chip and socket geometry, colours and transforms are unchanged; physical fit is unqualified.
TE models are for the 1- prefixed lead-free successors of the BOM part numbers; identical geometry is assumed.
The chip seating height (lead shoulders on the socket top, 5.10 mm) is assumed; TE customer drawings could not be retrieved.
TE models are single fused solids; contact faces that reach below the board are tin, while contact openings on top stay black.
Chip pins overlap the fused socket contacts inside the housing; this is hidden and not a fit claim.
Physical fit is unqualified.
Body and lead geometry are the installed KiCad DIN0207 models, unchanged; not a measurement of the kit parts.
Band widths, positions, the first-band end and the band colour values are illustrations; band order and values come from the original parts page.
The 1% body colour is sampled from four uncalibrated parts-page photographs; the 5% tan comes from the page band graphic, not a photograph.
R16 and R106 are banded per the parts page (150 ohm 5%, 24.0K 1%); their PCB values (100, 27K) are left unchanged.
The 40 LED resistors carry their PCB value (10K); the parts page says the value may vary.
Original CC0 illustrations from the XRL datasheet table and drawing; not manufacturer CAD or a measurement of the fitted historical parts.
Expanded-BOM part numbers come from search-engine extracts of a page that could not be read directly; the 100uF 10V/25V assignment is inferred from the parts page and its photographs.
Sleeve and stripe colours are sampled from uncalibrated photographs; printed value text is omitted.

The seat gaps (1.5 mm for 5 mm cans, whose leads are formed from 2.0 to 2.54 mm; 0.5 mm otherwise), lead forming, top disc, vent cross and 2.5 mm lead tip are illustrations; the datasheet allows +/-1 mm diameter and +/-1.5 mm length.
PCB value fields (47/16, 100/6.3, 1000/6.3) differ from the parts page and are left unchanged.
PTC end tapers, bands,0.4mm body standoff,0.75mm lead bends and trimmed tails are installation illustrations.
PTC table has no dimensional tolerances; TCR/band-code and actual thermal coupling remain unqualified.
Spacer central bore/end-land radii are illustrative and compliant retention tabs omitted.
Original0.24-inch BOM versus0.22-inch sequencer spacer height remains unresolved.
Terminal thicknesses, bends and several widths are labelled assumptions in terminal_spec.py.
Nominal-fit findings record drawing/footprint disagreements; neither source was altered.
USB pin stock, board-lock shape, insulation skirts and gold-strip dimensions remain illustrative; hidden contact routing is omitted.
Grayhill optional bracket holes and SDS-50J locating details remain as documented.
Recorded DRC warnings (silkscreen overlaps and edge clearance, dangling track stubs carried from the Eagle source) and schematic-parity warnings remain unchanged.

Two GND connection items remain by design: the original analog/digital mainboard ground split and the I/O jack-ground island, both unrouted airwires in the original Eagle boards and joined through the J3-J7 board-to-board wiring.
The B3F-40XX internal strips (1-2, 3-4) follow the original Eagle symbol and the design's use of them; the Omron drawing itself was not retrieved.
Gerber differences from the original Eagle CAM semantics are recorded, not corrected: SIP9 pad length, reference-label positions and names, NPTH stop frame, SMD mask corner radius and via tenting.
Eagle polygon pours are compared by outline, settings and connectivity; Eagle 4.13 pour fill geometry (thermal spokes, isolation) was not regenerated.
Nominal model checks and the Gerber comparison do not establish physical assembly; fabrication equivalence is to the original Eagle data, not to an inspected production board.
